summary: Capture the validated same-response supplier wallet request ID, retain completion identity separately, and bind private settlement evidence to the wallet correlation ID without SQL or grant changes.

review.scope: Independent 18-runtime-test rerun, source review, and exact single CI-path addition. The 13 SQL checks were run by the implementation worker.

behavior: x-request-id is captured only from the exact successful provider response and must be a single valid UUID; malformed or multiple values remain ambiguous and are never retried.
Completion ID, model and usage validation remain mandatory and unchanged.
The immutable settlement reference prefers usage:<providerRequestId>; providerRequestId and providerCompletionId are retained only in private usage_json.
Missing headers preserve the legacy completion-ID reference; no correlation ID is fabricated.
Customer result content contains neither supplier identifier; replay remains exactly one original dispatch.
Existing receipt SQL continues to bind owner, provider-key reference, exact model and immutable usage reference, with exactly-once receipt and overrun controls.
limitations: No SQL migration, grants, customer credit adjustment, provider call or deployment performed by this worker.
This links future gateway requests to wallet-log receipts; it does not create a customer ledger row for the earlier direct supplier acceptance call.
An authoritative actual-CNY reader or separately verified owner ingestion remains required; header identity alone does not prove the amount.
Header format is restricted to the observed UUID contract. Other supplier formats need explicit validation before activation.

Live read-only preflight found the confirmed owner account with zero funded/available credits, no completed requests, inference disabled and no route manifest; these are distinct from direct supplier response/debit acceptance.
PGlite tests use one in-memory database connection and do not certify independent concurrent production transactions.
